answer: Each identity registers one low-power radio whose analog fingerprint, carrier offset and I/Q imbalance, is measured by three receivers beside a dune station, its onyx case etched with the reading and an ember lamp wired to its transmitter. Monthly, verifiers send a fresh nonce; it must broadcast within 10 seconds and receivers refuse signals whose fingerprint drifts beyond tolerance. Clones sharing one radio collapse to one fingerprint, so 1,000 Sybils need 1,000 radios at $85 each ($85,000) plus separate antennas. Trade-off: heat shifts fingerprints, needing seasonal rechecks.
